title: BuiltWorlds homepage: construction technology network and conferences
answer: BuiltWorlds is a membership network and events publisher for buildings and infrastructure professionals. Its homepage says it enables members to learn about trends and technology, share insights and make strategic connections. The most useful item for AI in construction is its annual AI/ML Conference, which it says explores AI and machine learning in the AEC/O industry, covering existing and emerging solutions, implementation strategies at project and enterprise levels, and case studies with lessons learned.

sections.body: BuiltWorlds publishes this page as the homepage of its Buildings and Infrastructure Membership Network. It is a landing page for a global network and for two annual events, the Buildings Conference and the AI/ML Conference. The text states no publication date. It mentions a 2026 AI/ML Conference session in a headline. Its scope is buildings and infrastructure professionals, with conference topics in development, design, materials, systems, data centers, AI infrastructure, and AI/ML in AEC/O.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents BuiltWorlds as a member fueled network for buildings and infrastructure professionals. It says the network helps members learn about important trends and technology, share insights, and make strategic connections to adapt and succeed in a changing world. It describes two annual conferences. The Buildings Conference explores innovation and emerging technology in the development, design, materials, and systems of buildings, with a specific emphasis on data centers and AI infrastructure. It examines the current state and trajectory of building planning and operational solutions, strategies, and processes, and provides insights and guidance on implementation, use cases, opportunities, and challenges. The AI/ML Conference explores the growing and increasingly complicated landscape of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in the AEC/O industry. It provides context on the evolving role of AI/ML, details on existing and emerging solutions and use cases across all areas of the construction, building and operation process, strategies for implementation at project and enterprise levels, and case studies showing how companies use specific solutions and what they learned. The page also lists a session titled Quick Wins, Lasting Change: Founders Showcasing AI's Practical Power in Construction, under a Building Ventures Spotlight at the 2026 AI/ML Conference.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numerical figures beyond the year 2026 in a conference session listing. It describes BuiltWorlds as a global network for buildings and infrastructure professionals and describes the AI/ML Conference as covering AI and machine learning in the AEC/O industry. It positions the Buildings Conference as having a specific emphasis on data centers and AI infrastructure.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in construction can use this source to identify BuiltWorlds as a network and event organizer that tracks AI and machine learning in AEC/O. The page points to an annual AI/ML Conference as a place where solutions, use cases, implementation strategies and case studies are discussed. It also shows that AI infrastructure and data centers are a stated emphasis of the Buildings Conference. The page is useful mainly as a signpost to those programs and events rather than as a detailed research report.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Construction

sections.body: This is a homepage or landing page, so it gives little substantive detail. It does not provide research findings, data, methodology, pricing, membership terms, or dates for the conferences beyond a 2026 session mention. It is promotional in tone and describes itself as premier. It does not cover construction AI outside the AEC/O conference framing or give independent evidence for its claims.
